arch_opening: There is an update available — version 1.9.0. The theme is 'the writer never held the rule': v1.8.0 told the Architect to rotate BUILD-LOG, but the Builder writes it, and a Builder subagent starts with fresh context that never contains the Architect's rules. On a real project the log hit 1185 lines before anyone noticed. This release makes the size check mechanical, gives the Builder a length budget, and fixes rotation to aim at a target instead of moving the oldest entry. I'll look at your files and walk you through exactly what applies.

changes.title: BUILD-LOG size is checked by the Mechanical Gate, not by noticing
changes.what_changed: RULES.md ships with one pre-filled Mechanical Gate row: `awk 'END{exit (NR>400)}' handoff/BUILD-LOG.md`. It is the only gate command the framework provides — every other row is drafted from the project's own tooling.
changes.old_behavior: v1.8.0's rotation rule triggered on 'the file passes ~300 lines', which required the Architect to decide to run wc -l. Nothing computed it. On the project this was measured against, rotation fired once, opportunistically, while the Architect was idle waiting for the Reviewer — at 1185 lines, self-described as 'overdue since last session'.
changes.new_behavior: The Builder runs the gate before every review request, so the size ceiling is enforced once per step. Failing the row is not a code defect — the Builder signals the Architect, who rotates.
changes.user_impact_plain: The handoff log can drift by at most one step instead of a whole session, and nobody has to remember to check.
changes.how_to_assess: Read the project's RULES.md Mechanical Gate table. If it has no handoff-size row, offer to add it above the project's own checks. If the project has no RULES.md at all, that is a v1.7.0 change that never landed — install it first (templates/project-folder/RULES.md, or the clone's ./upgrade).
changes.user_decision: Want me to add the handoff-size row to your Mechanical Gate? It adds one command to what the Builder already runs.

changes.title: Builder gets a BUILD-LOG entry budget
changes.what_changed: BUILDER.md 'When You Are Done' now sets a 60-line target for the BUILD-LOG step entry and says explicitly that proof transcripts, command output, curl dumps, and gate evidence belong in REVIEW-REQUEST.md.
changes.old_behavior: BUILDER.md said only 'Update handoff/BUILD-LOG.md — step status, files changed, key decisions', with no length guidance. Measured entries ran 150-207 lines each.
changes.new_behavior: Step entries stay near 60 lines; the evidence still exists, in the file built to hold it.
changes.user_impact_plain: This is the source of the growth, not the cleanup. At ~180 lines per step against a 300-line threshold, no rotation cadence can keep up; at 60 the threshold holds for several steps.
changes.how_to_assess: Read the user's Builder role file (name from manifest.md). If its done-step lacks the length budget, offer the same edit the v1.9.0 template carries, preserving their team names and personas. Also skim their BUILD-LOG: entries far over 60 lines are the backlog this prevents, not something to rewrite retroactively.
changes.user_decision: Want me to add the entry budget to your Builder file? Existing log entries stay as they are — this only shapes new ones.

changes.title: Rotate to a target, not by age
changes.what_changed: The Architect's Anti-Drift rotation rule now says: keep moving entries out until BUILD-LOG is under 200 lines. It also drops the '~300 lines' perceptual trigger in favor of the gate row, and adds a write-once rule — a Known Gap is written once in the Known Gaps section and referenced by id from step entries, never restated.
changes.old_behavior: The rule said what to move (completed steps, closed gaps, full Lesson text) but not how far down to get. A correctly executed rotation on the measured project moved the oldest steps and finished at 385 lines — over threshold on completion — then regrew to 752 within twelve hours.
changes.new_behavior: Rotation aims at a number, so the file has headroom for the next few steps instead of sitting at the line.
changes.user_impact_plain: Stops the 'we just rotated and it's already overdue' cycle.
changes.how_to_assess: Read the user's Architect role file Anti-Drift section. If its rotation bullet has no target line count, offer the v1.9.0 wording. If their BUILD-LOG is currently over 400 lines, offer to run the rotation now — it is a move into handoff/archive/BUILD-LOG-<YYYY-MM>.md, never a delete; verify the moved text is byte-identical in the archive before removing it from the log.
changes.user_decision: Want me to update the rotation rule, and rotate your BUILD-LOG now if it is over the line?

changes.title: The gate row uses awk, not wc, on purpose
changes.what_changed: The shipped size check is written `awk 'END{exit (NR>400)}' handoff/BUILD-LOG.md` rather than `test "$(wc -l < handoff/BUILD-LOG.md)" -le 400`.
changes.old_behavior: The wc form was the obvious way to write it. Tested against a missing BUILD-LOG it exits 2 under bash and sh, but 0 under zsh — the empty command substitution compares as an integer — reporting a green gate for a handoff log that is not there.
changes.new_behavior: The awk form exits non-zero for oversized, missing, and unreadable alike, in bash, zsh, and sh.
changes.user_impact_plain: A check that reports green when its subject is absent is worse than no check. This is L-1's own rule — run every gate command in the failure environment before trusting it — applied to the framework's own gate command.
changes.how_to_assess: If the project already added a handoff-size row by hand using wc, offer to swap it for the awk form and say why. The reasoning is written into RULES.md so it does not get 'simplified' back.
changes.user_decision: Nothing to decide unless you already hand-rolled this check — then I'd swap it.

changes.title: Codex installs get a manifest.md — the version check never worked without one
changes.what_changed: setup-project.sh now installs manifest.md, stamping the version from the bundled releases registry at install time rather than from the template's own text. check-consistency.sh asserts the template's version matches the registry latest.
changes.old_behavior: setup-project.sh scaffolded AGENTS.md, role stubs, RULES.md and the handoff files but never installed manifest.md. check-version.py therefore printed 'Current version: unknown (no manifest.md)' followed by 'Run setup-project.sh to create a manifest' — the script that does not create it. The template that should have been installed had drifted to v1.5.0 across four releases, unnoticed, because nothing consumed it.
changes.new_behavior: A fresh Codex install carries a manifest stamped with the version it was installed from, and the offline version check reports correctly.
changes.user_impact_plain: Codex projects can tell what version they are on. Previously they could not, which also meant they never learned about critical updates.
changes.how_to_assess: This only affects Codex installs. Check whether the project root has a manifest.md. If not, the project was scaffolded by an older setup-project.sh — offer to create one, stamped with the version the project actually corresponds to (ask; do not guess from the latest registry entry, since the project may be several versions behind).
changes.user_decision: Codex projects only: want me to add the missing manifest.md so version checks start working?
